confirmed_gaps.observed: Compile rc=0, but at runtime: AttributeError: chain. IR lowers `itertools.chain(a,b)` to py_obj_getattr(<"itertools" string-literal placeholder @.pystr.obj.1>, @.pyattr.chain) then py_obj_call; getattr on the module-name string has no 'chain' attribute -> raises. Contrast: itertools.product(...) emits a clean direct call `user_itertools_product(...)` and works; itertools.islice/count/repeat (module-level functions) work; itertools.chain.from_iterable(nested) also works. ONLY calling the module-level instance `chain` via its __call__ fails.
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: pcc/frontends/python/codegen/native_modules.py::_maybe_emit_native_module_alias_call (around line 2766) handles only kind=='function' and kind=='class'; for kind=='module_global' it hits `if kind != "class": return None` and returns None, so the call falls through to generic dynamic dispatch which does py_obj_getattr on the module-name string placeholder -> AttributeError. In pcc/stdlib/itertools.py `chain = _Chain()` is a module-level INSTANCE, classified kind=='module_global' (DynType) by pipeline.py:4671 (vs `product`/`islice`/`count`/`repeat` which are `def`s -> kind=='function'). The defining module's init `_pcc_py_module_top_itertools()` DOES build the _Chain instance and store it into the extern global @.modvar.itertools.chain (verified IR lines 11027-11031), and _emit_native_module_export_value already loads kind=='module_global' from that global. The fix wires the call site to load the module_global value and py_obj_call it.

confirmed_gaps.observed: Compile rc=0, but at runtime: NameError: name 'filter' is not defined. Both `for v in filter(None, xs)` and `list(filter(None, xs))` fail. IR shows `@.name_error.1 = "name 'filter' is not defined"` and a `py_obj_call(<filter as name>, ...)` -> the `filter` builtin has no value/iterator-object form in the no-libpython runtime; it is only handled inline by the `next(filter(...))` consumer (iterator_builtin_lowering.py::_maybe_emit_next_filter_builtin, which DOES handle the None predicate via py_obj_truthy).
confirmed_gaps.root_cause: `filter(None, iterable)` (None predicate == keep-truthy) is not lowered by the list()/comprehension consumers. pcc/frontends/python/codegen/list_builtin_lowering.py::_maybe_emit_list_from_map_filter requires call.args[0] to be a Name (a function reference) and returns None when args[0] is NoneLit, so `list(filter(None, xs))` falls through and `filter` resolves as an unbound name -> NameError. The for-loop form `for v in filter(None, xs)` is a SEPARATE consumer (generic expr eval of the for-source) that likewise has no `filter` handler and hits the same NameError. The runtime has no general `filter` object; only next(filter(...)) is inlined. The bounded apply-ready fix below covers the list()/comprehension consumer by handling the None predicate with each element's own truthiness (same as the working next(filter(None,...)) path). NOTE: the for-loop consumer needs a parallel for-normalization handler (not included here) — same root cause, different dispatch site (for_normalization_lowering.py, alongside the existing enumerate/zip normalizers).

        mode = call.func.ident
        # ``filter(None, src)`` — the None predicate means "keep truthy

        pred_is_none = mode == "filter" and isinstance(call.args[0], NoneLit)
